topic: Understanding Distribution Channels – Concept & Progress
t: Which of the following is a 'flow' in a marketing channel that moves backward from customer to producer?
e: Payment and order flows move backward from customer to producer; physical, title and promotion flows move forward. Information flows in both directions.

topic: Understanding Distribution Channels – Concept & Progress
t: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India was constituted under an Act passed in:
e: The IRDA Act, 1999 created the regulator that subsequently framed the regulations governing all insurance distribution channels in India.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: 'Channel length' refers to:
o: The number of intermediaries between producer and customer
The duration of the channel contract
e: Longer channels have more levels of intermediaries; shorter channels give more control and faster feedback but need more producer investment.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: Which situation favours a SHORT (direct) channel?
o: Products are complex, high-value, customised and require technical selling
Customers are geographically dispersed and numerous
Products are low-value, standardised and bought frequently in small quantities
e: Complex, high-value products need direct contact and expertise; low-value, widely bought products and resource-constrained producers favour longer channels.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: 'Reward power' in a channel is exercised when a producer:
o: Offers extra incentives or support to intermediaries for performing desired functions
e: Reward power uses benefits (bonuses, contests, marketing support); coercive power uses threats, legitimate power uses contracts and referent power uses admiration.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: Which of the following is a disadvantage of multi-channel distribution?
o: Channel conflict and inconsistent customer experience across channels
e: Multiple channels extend reach and fit segments, but risk cannibalisation, conflict over customers and pricing, and inconsistent service unless well coordinated.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: An insurer wants to assess the 'economic criterion' for a proposed channel. Which pair of measures is MOST relevant?
o: Number of competitors and GDP growth
Expected sales volume and cost of selling through the channel
e: The economic criterion compares the sales each alternative will generate with the costs of achieving them; control and adaptability are the other two criteria.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: An individual agent's appointment can be cancelled by the insurer if the agent:
o: Sells more than 100 policies in a year
Violates the code of conduct or is found guilty of fraud, misrepresentation or rebating
Refuses to sell a product he considers unsuitable
e: Insurers may cancel appointments for breaches of the code of conduct or disqualifications under Section 42(3); the agent is then placed on the IRDAI blacklist where applicable.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: The foreign direct investment limit in Indian insurance companies was raised to 74% by the Insurance (Amendment) Act of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). FDI was 26% from 2000, raised to 49% in 2015 and to 74% in 2021, to bring more capital for growth and distribution expansion.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Rebating is prohibited under which section of the Insurance Act, 1938?
e: Section 41 prohibits offering any rebate of premium or commission as inducement; Section 38 is assignment, Section 45 is non-contestability and Section 64VB is premium-in-advance.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A corporate agent in India is permitted to be registered in which categories?
o: Life, general, health, or a composite of these
e: Corporate agents may be registered as life, general, health or composite corporate agents, with the tie-up limit of nine insurers applying per category.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Which statement about insurance brokers is INCORRECT?
o: A broker's registration is valid for three years
A direct broker can also undertake reinsurance broking without separate registration
Brokers can place business with any registered insurer without tie-up limits
Brokers are remunerated by insurers within the EoM framework
e: Reinsurance broking requires registration as a reinsurance broker or composite broker with higher capital; a direct broker cannot do it. The other statements are correct.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: The application processing fee for a composite broker's registration is:
e: Processing fees are ₹25,000 (direct), ₹50,000 (reinsurance) and ₹75,000 (composite); renewal fees are ₹1 lakh, ₹3 lakh and ₹5 lakh respectively.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A joint-venture bancassurance model is one where:
o: The bank sells insurance without registration
The bank refers customers for a fee
The bank and an insurance company jointly promote an insurer, sharing ownership and strategy (e.g. SBI Life)
e: Joint ventures sit between pure distribution alliances and full integration; several Indian life insurers were promoted jointly by banks and foreign insurers.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A DEMERIT of bancassurance from the insurer's perspective is that:
o: The insurer depends on the bank's priorities, and the bank may switch partners or give insurance low attention versus core banking products
e: Insurers lack control over bank staff and may lose the channel when tie-ups change; with open architecture, banks can also shift volumes among nine partners.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: The minimum professional indemnity cover for a web aggregator is:
e: Web aggregators must carry PI insurance of twice annual remuneration subject to a minimum of ₹25 lakh and a maximum of ₹100 crore.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Which of the following activities may an IMF undertake in addition to insurance solicitation?
o: Issuing policies in its own name
Distribution of other financial products such as mutual funds and pension products, and insurance servicing activities like survey/loss assessment
e: IMFs are designed as area-based financial-services distributors; they may market other regulated products and perform permitted servicing functions, but not underwrite or reinsure.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: The IMF registration fee payable to IRDAI is:
e: IMFs pay ₹5,000 on registration and ₹2,000 on renewal, deliberately kept low to encourage small, district/State-level firms.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A POSP-Life pure term product allows which entry age and minimum policy term?
o: Minimum entry age 25 and minimum term 10 years
Minimum entry age 18 and minimum term 5 years
Minimum entry age 18 and minimum term 1 year
e: POS pure term products: minimum entry age 18, maximum maturity age 65, minimum term 5 years, sum assured in multiples of ₹50,000 with non-medical underwriting.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: An insurer sells the same term plan through its website at a premium 10% lower than through agents. Agents complain that customers meet them for advice and then buy online. This is an example of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Conflict between different channel types serving the same market (agents versus the insurer's own online channel) is multi-channel conflict; horizontal conflict would be between two agents.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Which of the following is a merit of the micro-insurance agent channel?
o: Reaches low-income groups through trusted community institutions (SHGs, NGOs, MFIs) at low cost
e: Micro-insurance agents leverage existing community relationships to distribute small-ticket products, supporting rural and social sector obligations.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: The service-quality 'delivery gap' occurs when:
o: Service standards exist but frontline staff and channels fail to perform to them
e: The delivery gap is between specifications and actual performance; it is addressed through training, supervision and incentives for distributors.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: 'Personnel benefit' as a component of customer value refers to:
o: The competence, courtesy and credibility of the people the customer deals with
e: The agent's knowledge, responsiveness and trustworthiness are personnel benefits; image benefit comes from the insurer's brand and reputation.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: Which of the following best illustrates distribution adding 'service benefit' for a health insurance customer?
o: The agent coordinates cashless hospitalisation pre-authorisation with the TPA on the customer's behalf
e: Support in using the policy (claims coordination, reminders, endorsements) is a service benefit that increases total customer benefit beyond the core product.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: A bank customer buying a policy at the branch must wait 45 minutes and fill a 10-page paper form. In value terms this mainly:
o: Increases time and energy costs, reducing perceived value
e: Delays and effort are non-monetary costs; reducing them through digital on-boarding is a key value lever for bancassurance.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: The 'tangibles' dimension of SERVQUAL for an insurer would include:
o: Appearance of offices, equipment, staff and communication materials
e: Tangibles are the physical and visual evidence of service; the other options correspond to reliability, assurance and responsiveness.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: 'Variability' (heterogeneity) of services affects insurance distribution because:
o: Service quality depends on who delivers it and when, so standardisation through training and scripts is needed
e: Heterogeneity means the customer experience varies with the individual distributor; insurers counter it with standard sales processes, training and quality audits.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: Which of the following is a CHALLENGE unique to distributing long-term savings-oriented life insurance?
o: Customers must be persuaded to commit to paying premiums for many years, and returns are visible only far in the future
e: Deferred benefits and long premium-paying terms make the sale harder and persistency critical; the distributor must build trust and manage expectations.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: IRDAI's stated vision 'Insurance for All' targets the year:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). IRDAI aims for every citizen to have appropriate life, health and property cover and every enterprise to have suitable insurance by 2047, the centenary of India's independence.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: A life insurer's agency force of 50,000 produced ₹5,000 crore of new business premium in a year, while its 200 corporate agents produced ₹4,000 crore. The average productivity per agent and per corporate agent respectively are:
e: ₹5,000 crore ÷ 50,000 = ₹10 lakh per agent; ₹4,000 crore ÷ 200 = ₹20 crore per corporate agent. Productivity comparisons guide channel investment decisions.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: 'Insurtech' creates distribution opportunities primarily through:
o: Digital onboarding, data analytics, API-based embedded distribution and automated underwriting that lower cost to serve
e: Technology reduces the cost of acquiring and servicing small-ticket customers, enabling new channels and partnerships (e-commerce, fintech, telecom).

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: Low financial literacy in India affects insurance distribution by:
o: Increasing dependence on trusted intermediaries and raising the risk of mis-selling, so simple products and plain-language disclosure are needed
e: Where customers cannot evaluate products, the distributor's advice dominates the decision; this is both an opportunity (advice is valued) and a conduct risk.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: Which statement about pricing and the channel is CORRECT in insurance?
o: Agents may quote any premium they choose
Premium rates are set by the insurer (filed under Use and File) and cannot be altered by the distributor, unlike dealer pricing in goods
Brokers fix premium rates for the market
Premiums vary by the agent's commission preference
e: Insurance intermediaries cannot change the price of the product; competition between channels is on advice, service and convenience, not on premium discounts.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: 'Social sector' lives for the purpose of IRDAI obligations include:
o: Unorganised-sector workers, economically vulnerable or backward classes and persons with disabilities
e: The rural and social sector obligations push insurers to design channels (micro-insurance agents, CSCs, Bima Vahaks) that reach these under-served groups.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: A key objective of CRM in insurance distribution is to:
o: Increase customer retention, share of wallet and lifetime value through consistent, personalised engagement
e: CRM shifts focus from transactions to relationships: keeping customers longer, selling them more and turning them into advocates.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: An insurer surveys 1,000 customers; 550 give scores of 9–10, 250 give 7–8 and 200 give 0–6. Its Net Promoter Score is:
e: NPS = %Promoters − %Detractors = 55% − 20% = +35. Passives (25%) are excluded from the calculation.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: 'Share of wallet' refers to:
o: The market share of the insurer
The proportion of a customer's total spending in a category that goes to a particular company
e: CRM aims to increase share of wallet by cross-selling and up-selling to existing customers, which is cheaper than acquiring new ones.

topic: Principles
t: The principle that allows an insurer who has paid a claim to step into the insured's shoes and recover from a liable third party is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Subrogation is a corollary of indemnity; it does not apply to life or personal accident (benefit) policies.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: A life insurer uses a predictive model flagging policies likely to lapse and asks agents to contact those customers before the premium due date. This is an example of:
o: Analytical CRM feeding operational action for retention
e: Analytics identify at-risk customers; the operational channel then acts on the insight — a typical integrated CRM loop that improves persistency.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: Which of the following practices weakens customer relationships?
o: Sending policy anniversary greetings and need reviews
Providing a single point of contact for service
Contacting the customer only when a new product is to be sold
e: Relationship marketing requires regular, value-adding contact; purely sales-driven contact erodes trust and leads to churn.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: KYC norms in insurance distribution require the distributor to:
o: Ignore identity documents for small policies
Collect KYC only at claim stage
Verify the identity and address of the proposer (e.g. through Aadhaar-based e-KYC, PAN or other officially valid documents) at the time of proposal
e: KYC is mandatory for all new policies under anti-money-laundering guidelines; digital KYC (e-KYC, video KYC, CKYC) has made it faster for distributors.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: The Insurance Self-Network Platform (ISNP) guidelines allow:
o: Agents to set up their own insurance companies
Insurers and intermediaries to sell and service policies through their own approved online platforms
Customers to sell policies to each other
e: ISNP guidelines (2017) govern e-commerce platforms of insurers and intermediaries, prescribing security, disclosure and e-proposal standards for online distribution.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: Which of the following is a best practice in managing channel partners such as banks?
o: A clear agreement with service standards, joint business plans, dedicated relationship managers and regular performance reviews
Leaving all training to the bank
e: Structured partner management (SLAs, joint planning, training support, MIS reviews) sustains bancassurance productivity and compliance.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: Grievance redressal best practice requires the insurer to:
o: Treat complaints as agent problems only
Acknowledge and resolve complaints within prescribed timelines, inform the customer of escalation to the Ombudsman, and analyse complaint data to fix root causes
e: IRDAI's policyholder-protection framework prescribes timelines and escalation; analysing complaint patterns by channel helps correct sales-process weaknesses.

topic: Principles
t: In a life insurance contract, insurable interest must exist:
o: At the time of the claim only
Both at inception and at claim
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Life: at inception only. Marine: at the time of loss. Fire and motor: at both inception and loss.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: Which of the following is NOT one of the IRDAI initiatives described for expansion of insurance in India?
e: IRDAI's recent initiatives are liberalising and technology-driven; nationalisation runs counter to the reforms that opened the sector in 2000.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: Bima Sugam is expected to benefit distribution by:
o: Providing a single digital platform where customers can compare, buy, renew, port and claim across insurers, with intermediaries also able to operate on it
e: The marketplace aims at transparency and lower cost of distribution, while agents, brokers and others can still serve customers through the platform.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: A general insurer with GWP ₹800 crore incurs ₹260 crore of expenses of management including commission. Compared with the EoM limit, the insurer is:
e: Limit = 30% × ₹800 crore = ₹240 crore; actual ₹260 crore exceeds it by ₹20 crore, which the insurer must address through its board-approved plan.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: The 2022 reform allowing IMFs to tie up with more insurers and operate across a State was intended to:
o: Make the IMF model more viable and widen choice for customers in smaller towns
e: Wider tie-ups and area of operation improve IMF economics, supporting the regulator's goal of deeper distribution outside large cities.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: Which of the following best describes IRDAI's approach to 'open architecture' in distribution?
o: Allowing agents to sell any insurer's product without appointment
Requiring every insurer to have an open-plan office
Allowing corporate agents and IMFs to tie up with multiple insurers per category so that customers get choice at the point of sale
e: Open architecture expanded in 2015 (three insurers per category) and further in 2022 (nine for corporate agents, six for IMFs); individual agents remain tied to one insurer per category.
